summary: Charleston County tower on the SC Forestry Commission list; the only tower-specific item is a July 1949 towerlady notice. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: No source read says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: Forest Lookouts quotes a July 15, 1949 Aiken Standard item naming Mrs. Thelma Garvin as towerlady at Adams Run Tower

evidence.supports: Charleston County, South Carolina Forestry Commission tower
evidence.quote: South Carolina - Charleston County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Listed under Charleston County, South Carolina Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: Charleston County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Towerlady named in a July 15, 1949 Aiken Standard item (as quoted by Forest Lookouts), third prize in the 1948-49 contest
evidence.quote: July 15, 1949: Mrs. Thelma Garvin, Towerlady at Adams Run Tower in Charleston county, awarded third prize in the 1948-49 Towersite Improvement contest. (Aiken Standard)

evidence.supports: First Forestry Commission fire tower erected August 1930 near Camden
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.

evidence.supports: Many early towers built from wooden beams
evidence.quote: many of the early South Carolina towers were built from wooden beams

evidence.supports: Steel eventually replaced all wooden towers
evidence.quote: Eventually, all wooden towers were replaced by steel structures.

evidence.supports: Towers not routinely manned at night (statewide)
evidence.quote: Towers were not routinely manned at night.

evidence.supports: Most operators from the 1960s on were women, often married to firefighters (statewide)
evidence.quote: From the 1960s on, most South Carolina tower operators were women; frequently their husbands were employed as firefighters.
In many cases, the tower became a family tradition, with adult children succeeding their parents as tower operators.

evidence.supports: State closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993 (statewide)
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific fact is the 1949 towerlady notice, quoted on Forest Lookouts from the Aiken Standard; the original newspaper was not read. Build date, design, height, staffing after 1949, fire history, fate and site condition are not in any source read, so the story leaves them out apart from the statewide context. The statewide closure date is not a finding about this tower. The brief's coordinates are not from a source here, and the brief's status and access stay unknown. The NHLR South Carolina index in the cache has no Adams Run entry. Two searches and about four page reads.
